name: deeprec
axis: deep LINEAR NON-TAIL recursion (5_000 live frames per call) — stack depth + return-path cost
notes: 600M calls total (120_000 x 5_000). Paired with bench/recursion/tailcall: identical depth, identical op count, the ONLY difference is that the combine here happens after the call returns. Two design forces, both found by measurement: (1) the first draft `n + sumTo(n-1)` summing to 10_000 was VOID — rustc folded the whole program to a constant (1.3ms == startup) because sum_to is pure and loop-invariant, and separately LLVM's accumulator-recursion transform turns `n + f(n-1)` into a LOOP (verified: idiomatic Rust `sum_to` completes at depth 100_000_000). The shipped body `f(n-1) * 3 + n` is not reassociable, so all four genuinely recurse — verified by Rust's stack overflow at depth ~500-600k. (2) `seed` threads the caller's accumulator in so the call is not loop-invariant and cannot be hoisted. Depth is 5_000 rather than 10_000 because deno INTERMITTENTLY threw RangeError at 10_000 depending on ambient stack use; VL was stable at 10_000. MAX RECURSION DEPTH for this exact function, measured by bisection: rust ~500_000-600_000 (8MiB main stack), VL/wasmtime 16_210, deno/V8 15_625, CPython 998 (default sys.getrecursionlimit()=1000, NOT raised). Scale-verified at N and N/2: rust 0.512, deno 0.486, vl 0.496 (expected 0.500). Min-of-3 on core 6: rust 0.691s, vl 1.061s, deno 2.403s, python 0.867s. VL is 2.26x FASTER than deno and 1.54x slower than rust. opt.vl (driver in a function, so locals not globals) measured 1.073s — 1% SLOWER than main.vl, i.e. the top-level-let global cliff does not appear here either.

startupBaselineSeconds._measured: min-of-10, empty program, taskset -c 6, contended 24-core i9-12900KF

compileTime._note: compile time, measured separately and never inside an execution number

consolidatedRun._method: single interleaved pass over ALL 8 recursion benchmarks, min-of-3, taskset -c 6, per-runtime empty-program startup subtracted, machine contended by other agents (loadavg ~10) so read the RATIOS not the absolutes

audit.pythonIsADifferentWorkload: Python changes BOTH knobs (depth 5000->900 AND repeats 120000->10000 = 66.7x less work) and at depth 900 it is no longer exercising the deep-stack axis the benchmark exists for. Correctly disclosed in depth/depthPython, but there is no single scalar normalisation factor — do not quote a normalised Python number for this benchmark.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
